llm.summary: This is a Jimeng prompt-writing skill, but it needs review because a bundled memory file still tells the agent to save preferences automatically despite consent promises elsewhere.

dimensions.detail: Reading and writing a local preference file is purpose-aligned, but automatic cross-session read/reinjection plus broad activation creates a real risk of unexpected profile use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The documented install path is the normal OpenClaw skill install command; no post-install scripts, package managers, or remote payload retrieval were present in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill has broad trigger phrases such as generic image-generation requests, and its main instructions conflict with the memory reference about whether preference writes require consent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and PRIVACY.md require consent before writing, but references/evolution-memory.md says each session is automatically appended; this undercuts the consent-gated privacy model.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core prompt-engineering workflow for Jimeng/Seedance/Seedream is coherent, and the package is Markdown-only with no executable scripts, dependencies, credential collection, or external upload mechanism found.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with local cross-session visual preference memory. Before relying on it, review or disable references/evolution-memory.md, require an explicit yes before every write, and periodically inspect or delete stored preferences.
llm.findings:
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language prompts and docs fit a Chinese Jimeng-focused skill, so this is not a security verdict driver by itself; however, consent and privacy text being Chinese-only is worth user caution.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad trigger examples can invoke the skill for ordinary image-generation requests that do not explicitly mention Jimeng, which compounds the memory concern.
[SDI-1] expected: Local visual preference memory is an advertised feature, but cross-session reinjection should depend on the stated consent model.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The main files do provide privacy notices, but the memory reference itself lacks the same consent warning and instead describes automatic persistence.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The automatic-append instruction is directly inconsistent with the consent-gated write rules in SKILL.md and PRIVACY.md.
[T09] unexpected: The static finding is supported as a local persistence and consent-conflict issue, not as code execution, privilege escalation, or exfiltration.
